_note: Append a new snapshot each time an authority (SINAPROC, MINSA, Presidencia) publishes figures. null = not reported.

snapshots.note: No consolidated official balance yet. Sinaproc director Omar Smith reported 'several injured' (no figure) and damage concentrated in Veraguas, Herrera and Los Santos (Chitré, Venao). No deaths confirmed by any authority. At least 1 injured in Penonomé market (El Siglo/Infobae). Claims of trapped people at El Sitio hostel, Playa Venao, unconfirmed.

snapshots.source_name: SINAPROC (deputy director Malitzie Rivera / director Omar Smith), as reported by media
snapshots.note: Sinaproc says no deaths recorded. 'Several' injured were taken to hospitals in the central provinces, but no number was given. As of ~21:30Z no consolidated figures for injured, displaced or damaged homes had been published. Also cited at 16:24 local in El Tiempo's live blog: https://www.eltiempo.com/mundo/latinoamerica/fuerte-terremoto-en-panama-reportan-sismo-de-magnitud-8-0-durante-la-tarde-de-este-viernes-9-de-octubre-hay-alerta-de-tsunami-3592581 . CSS (Social Security) separately reported no injured patients, users or staff in its facilities (La Estrella, existing report u202610092103_4).

snapshots.source_name: SINAPROC / Ministerio de Gobierno — Comunicado Oficial N° 1
snapshots.note: Comunicado Oficial N° 1 (9 Oct 2026; time not stated, recorded 17:58 local): no deaths; 'some people injured' without a total (incl. 15 students with minor injuries at Escuela Alberto Zúñiga, Coclé); no missing persons reported; 47+ aftershocks (IGC-UP). Damage to government buildings, roads, churches, hotels, shops and homes in Azuero, Coclé, Panamá, Darién and Chiriquí; water treatment plants damaged nationwide (Chilibre at 20%).

snapshots.source_name: SINAPROC consolidated report (cut-off 20:00 local), reported by La Prensa / EFE
snapshots.note: SINAPROC consolidated report (cut-off 20:00 local, 9 Oct): 0 dead, 0 missing, 27 with minor injuries; 142 homes affected, at least 3 destroyed (Herrera 2, Chiriquí 1); 188 schools, 20 health facilities, 26 government buildings, 13 churches, 7 hotels, 9 bridges and 4 residential buildings affected; ~300 people evacuated from Isla Cañas as a precaution; 8 families sheltered in Coclé (EFE).

snapshots.source_name: Government of Panama / SINAPROC (Cabinet press conference, 10 Oct)
snapshots.note: Cabinet declared a national state of emergency (focus on Herrera, Los Santos and Veraguas) and allocated US$100 million. SINAPROC: 0 deaths, 27 injured; more than 426 homes assessed with damage (severe, moderate, minor) by MOP, MIVIOT and SINAPROC, about 2,130 people affected (damnificados); 419 schools (MEDUCA) and 21 health facilities affected; 300 people evacuated from Isla Cañas. MEDUCA to decide on Sunday whether classes resume Monday.

snapshots.source_name: COE Nacional / SINAPROC report (~18:30 local, 10 Oct), as reported by TVN and La Prensa
snapshots.note: COE/SINAPROC national balance (Saturday ~18:30 local): 0 deaths, 0 missing, 29 injured; 840 homes affected (Herrera 206, Veraguas 202, Los Santos 182, Coclé 149, Chiriquí 49 incl. 10 destroyed, Panamá Oeste 21, Colón 18, Bocas del Toro 8, Darién 1) plus 4 apartment buildings; about 267 people in shelters (Mariato 255, Penonomé 12) and 300 evacuated as a precaution from Isla Cañas; 1,213 people registered as affected (the Cabinet cited ~2,130 damnificados); 419 schools; 11 bridges. Health facilities (21) from the Cabinet briefing the same day.

snapshots.source_name: SINAPROC Comunicado Oficial N.º 7 (via Retén Chiriquí)
snapshots.note: SINAPROC Communiqué No. 7 (as of 12:00, Sunday 11 Oct): 1,293 homes evaluated with damage; about 619 schools affected; no deaths and no missing persons; about 570 people in shelters (310+ in Veraguas, 257 in Colón); ~1,500 people affected in Los Santos; 66,000+ lbs of aid flown in and 170 tonnes of water distributed. The COE director says the count will rise as unreachable communities are assessed. Injured (29) and health facilities (21) from the previous national balance.

SINAPROC Communiqué No. 8 (11:30, Monday 12 Oct): 1,287 homes with damage (Veraguas 420, Coclé 318, Herrera 302, Colón 29, Chiriquí 28 total losses; Los Santos not itemised); 1,744 families evaluated; 598 people in 14 shelters; 656 schools affected (Veraguas 196, Chiriquí 139, Los Santos 71, Coclé 40, Colón 36, Darién 10); at least 28 health facilities (Veraguas 22, 3 hospitals in Herrera, Hospital San Juan in Colón; Telemetro reports 67 in total); 10 communities cut off (5 in Los Santos, 5 in Herrera) plus 4 islands in Veraguas; no deaths or missing. Government buildings (60+), churches (44) and hotels (11) from the national balance reported by Infobae. Injured (29) and bridges (11) from earlier balances. Local reports suggest undercounting: 400+ homes affected in Cañazas district alone (Telemetro).

snapshots.source_name: President Mulino, report to the Nation (12 Oct)
snapshots.note: President Mulino's report to the Nation (Monday evening 12 Oct): 6,174 people affected in 1,744 homes evaluated by UTP engineers, SINAPROC and US specialists; 35 schools destroyed (MEDUCA) of 656 affected; 67 of 842 health facilities damaged, US$61M needed for repairs, new hospital for Tonosí (MINSA); ~16 bridges damaged (Metas secretary: ~1,250 homes in first surveys); construction of the first 1,300 homes to start, prioritising the most vulnerable families. 7,100 security personnel, 1,100 SINAPROC staff and volunteers, 460 firefighters; 24,000 food bags; 240 t of water. Homes damaged (1,287), shelters (598) and injured (29) from SINAPROC Communiqué 8 and earlier balances.

SINAPROC report (22:00, Monday 12 Oct): 7,480 people affected in 2,164 families across nine provinces. Housing damage by family: 506 total loss, 507 moderate, 776 partial, 375 minor. 31 pregnant women and 290 people with disabilities among those affected. 35 schools collapsed (Herrera 20: Las Minas 13, Los Pozos 6, Ocú 1; Veraguas 7; Los Santos 5; Coclé 2; Chiriquí 1), affecting 422 students.

snapshots.source_name: Government briefing after Cabinet (J. R. Icaza), 13 Oct
snapshots.note: Government briefing after the Cabinet meeting (Tuesday 13 Oct, Minister J. R. Icaza): 11,460 people affected in 3,367 families evaluated; 2,841 people in 33+ shelters; 27 injured (minor to moderate), no deaths or missing; 28 patients airlifted; 1,250+ homes damaged, destroyed or uninhabitable (preliminary); 600+ public schools and ~90 government buildings affected; 121,000+ lb of aid by air and 331+ t of water. Homes damaged (2,164 families with housing damage) and destroyed (506 total losses) from SINAPROC's 12 Oct 22:00 report; schools (656), health facilities (67, MINSA) and bridges (~16) from earlier official figures. Counts keep rising as remote communities are assessed.

snapshots.source_name: SINAPROC Comunicado Oficial N.º 11 (via Retén Chiriquí)
snapshots.note: SINAPROC Communiqué No. 11 (19:00, Tuesday 13 Oct): 3,390 homes affected and 727 total losses (in Herrera and Los Santos); 11,527 people evaluated in 3,667 families, including 42 pregnant women and 452 people with disabilities; 2,841+ people in 33+ shelters (2,044 in Veraguas, 644 in Los Santos); 27 injured, no deaths or missing; 619 schools under evaluation and 35 collapsed (MEDUCA); 32 landslides and 11 communities cut off in Herrera. Provincial housing figures as reported (Los Santos 1,613, Coclé 1,052, Veraguas 614, Herrera 498, Colón 14) add up to more than the national total, so treat them as indicative. Minister Icaza: housing reports rose from ~1,200 to ~3,300 as families registered damage on the government platform; 66 health facilities damaged. Government buildings (~90), bridges (~16), churches and hotels from earlier official figures.

snapshots.source_name: COEN / SINAPROC consolidated report, 9–19 Oct (via La Estrella)
snapshots.note: COEN/SINAPROC consolidated report for 9–19 October: 9,124 homes evaluated: 2,318 with total damage (7,430 residents), 5,546 with moderate or partial damage (18,470 residents), 1,260 with minor damage (4,052 residents); 29,952 people affected, including 98 pregnant women and 1,194 people with disabilities; 3,827 people in 55 shelters, 2,672 of them (70%) in Veraguas; 576 schools, 42 health facilities, 44 churches, 87 public buildings and 69 roads and bridges damaged; 27 injured. Los Santos and Herrera account for 74% of home evaluations; Veraguas and Chiriquí for 55% of damaged schools. One death: Elena Barría (68), injured when her house collapsed in Macaracas, died in hospital on 14 Oct (CSS).

COE update (12:30, Tuesday 20 Oct, director René García): more than 10,100 homes and 33,200 people evaluated; 3,000+ homes classified red (uninhabitable or total loss), about 5,000 yellow (repairable), the rest green; 100+ pregnant women and 1,300 people with disabilities among those evaluated. Shelters (3,827 in 55), schools, health facilities, public buildings and churches from the 19 Oct consolidated report. One death (Elena Barría, 68, Macaracas, died 14 Oct). Figures are evaluations, not final damage counts; Panamá Conecta has received 8,000+ damage reports and MIVIOT lists 6,400+ homes affected.

SINAPROC balance (18:00, Wednesday 21 Oct): 11,321 homes evaluated: 2,890 total loss, 6,874 moderate or partial damage, 1,557 minor (Los Santos 5,060 and Herrera 3,267 evaluated); 37,210 people registered in damage and needs assessments (EDAN); 5,628 people (1,051 families) in 126 shelters, 3,531 of them in Veraguas; 27 injured; 2 deaths; 47 critical points and 23 bridges needing rehabilitation; IMA delivered 58,909 food bags to 750 communities.

Government briefing (18:30, Thursday 22 Oct, Minister J. R. Icaza and SINAPROC director Omar Smith): 12,333 homes affected with 40,791 residents; 3,129 homes with total damage; 6,654 people in 122 shelters; 576 schools affected; 775 communities assisted in five provinces. Deaths: Elena Barría (68, Macaracas, died 14 Oct) and Regina Miranda (60, school secretary in Santiago, injured while evacuating, died 22 Oct); La Prensa counts a third death of a person with pre-existing conditions. Homes are being tagged green (safe), yellow (restricted, repairs needed) or red (uninhabitable); a public map is available on panamaconecta.gob.pa. Health facilities (42), public buildings (87) and churches (44 official; 100+ according to the Catholic Church) from earlier reports; bridges = 23 needing rehabilitation (SINAPROC 21 Oct).

snapshots.source_name: COE balance, 9–24 Oct (via Telemetro / La Verdad)
snapshots.note: COE balance for 9–24 October (published 25 Oct): 13,985 homes evaluated: 3,390 total damage, 7,883 moderate or partial, 1,869 minor; 5,779 people in 154 active shelters (Los Santos 1,143 in 36; Herrera 675 in 39; most of the rest in Veraguas); 27 injured; 853 schools and 120 health centres inspected; IMA food aid to 1,304 communities. Deaths (2) from MINSA; people affected (40,791) from the 22 Oct briefing, not updated in this balance. Chiriquí: 300+ homes affected and ~1,200 people affected (TVN, 26 Oct).

conflicts: Magnitude: USGS M7.7 (initially 8.0, then 7.6), depth 12.6 km; IGC-UP M7.2 (initially 7.0), depth 4–10 km, located 39 km W/NW of Tonosí; SGC Colombia 7.3 then 8.0.
Epicentre province: USGS names Pitaloza Arriba (AP/Reuters say Herrera); local media cite Tonosí, Los Santos.

Collapsed hotel location: Panamanian media place it in Penonomé (Hotel Dos Continentes); BioBioChile wrongly reported a four-storey hotel in downtown Panama City; es.wikipedia/Infobae also mention a separate partial hotel collapse near Tonosí.
Some outlets (Vanguardia) wrongly call Penonomé the epicentre zone.

Aftershock counts differ by source and time: 46 by 15:00 and ~86 by 16:30 (Instituto de Geociencias), more than 100 by 17:30 (SINAPROC), at least 147 by ~22:15 (CNN, source not stated); 256 by Sunday 11 Oct, more than 350 by Monday morning and more than 400 by Monday afternoon 12 Oct (Instituto de Geociencias); an aftershock at 18:20 local on 12 Oct was M6.1 (USGS) / M6.4 (IGC), with 416 aftershocks located by 21:00; 1,056 by 26 Oct (IGC). On 27 Oct an M5.6–5.7 (IGC; USGS M5.0) aftershock near Coiba was felt in Panama City. The USGS catalogue lists only larger events; largest M6.6 (USGS) / M6.9 (IGC).
PorEsto claims damage to Puente Centenario; El Tiempo video shows only shaking, no damage reported.
Several outlets recycled Sinaproc text from the 10 Aug 2026 Colombia quake ('9:31 a.m. no persons affected') — not applicable to this event.

Injuries: Sinaproc director Omar Smith reported 'several injured' (no figure); the Caja de Seguro Social (15:27 local) said no patients, users or staff were affected in its own facilities. Neither is a national total.
Largest aftershock (20:25 UTC): USGS M6.6, 14 km W of Río Grande (Veraguas); IGC-UP M6.9, 32 km from Coiba; El Tiempo also cites M6.6 8 km NW of Río Grande.

USGS ShakeMap: version 10 (automatic, 12 Oct 19:54 UTC) re-calibrates the model with 'Did You Feel It?' reports and lowers intensities sharply (epicentre ~VI, Los Pozos ~V–VI, Soná ~III; people at MMI VII+ from ~550,000 to ~60,000). This contradicts observed damage (300+ homes collapsed in Los Pozos, church towers down, schools destroyed), so this platform keeps the earlier ShakeMap (v8) for its exposure and poverty analysis until USGS reviews the map.

Housing counts differ by source and method: SINAPROC field counts (1,287 homes on 12 Oct), self-registration on the government platform Panamá Conecta (3,300 by 14 Oct, 8,000+ reports by 20 Oct), MIVIOT (6,400+ homes) and COE technical evaluations (9,124 evaluated with 2,318 total damage by 19 Oct; 10,100 evaluated with 3,000+ red by 20 Oct). This platform shows the latest COE evaluation figures.

Deaths: the Health Ministry confirms two deaths from direct trauma (Elena Barría, 14 Oct; Regina Miranda, 22 Oct); La Prensa reports three, including a person with pre-existing conditions whose health worsened during the earthquake.
